claims.text: Special Night Squads: formed by Wingate, 'comprised primarily of Haganah fighters'; many he trained became heads of the Palmach and the IDF.
Jewish Supernumerary Police set up by the British in June 1936; 6,000 to 14,000 to 22,000; 'Those trained became the nucleus of the Haganah'; Jewish Settlement Police from 1938.
Village files compiled from the early 1940s by Haganah scouts and the Shai, catalogued by the general staff's planning bureau 'in preparation for a future conflict'.
Polish courses for Irgun members: 40 in summer 1938, 25 at Andrychów in spring 1939; about 20,000 rifles sent per one Polish account, part never delivered.
Pan York and Pan Crescent: bought in the US 1947; about 15,000 passengers from Burgas 27 Dec 1947; interned in Cyprus; the US threatened not to support partition if they sailed.
Palmach founded May 1941 for fear of a German invasion; more than 2,000 at first; about 7,000 served in the war; three of twelve Haganah brigades.
